question: What minimum vertical clearance is required for overhead signs over the pavement and shoulders?
model_answer: Direct Answer: Overhead signs must provide a vertical clearance of not less than 17 feet, measured to the sign, light fixture, or sign bridge, over the entire width of the pavement and shoulders. A lesser clearance is permitted where nearby structures already have a lower vertical clearance, and where overhead devices are placed above sidewalks, at least 7 feet of clearance to the sidewalk surface is required. Standards (mandatory): - "Overhead signs shall provide a vertical clearance of not less than 17 feet to the sign, light fixture, or sign bridge over the entire width of the pavement and shoulders, except where the structure on which the overhead signs are to be mounted or other structures along the roadway near the sign structure have a lesser vertical clearance." [shown on Page 100 image, Section 2A.15] - "Signs that are post-mounted on a median barrier that overhang any portion of the traveled way shall be mounted with a vertical clearance that complies with that of overhead signs." [shown on Page 100 image, Section 2A.15] - "If overhead traffic control devices are placed above sidewalks, the clearance from the bottom of the device to the sidewalk surface directly under the sign or device shall be at least 7 feet." - "Where lateral clearance is limited, Preferential Lane regulatory signs that are post-mounted on a median barrier and that are wider than 72 inches shall be mounted with a vertical clearance that complies with the provisions of Section 2A.15 for overhead mounting if any portion of the sign extends over the roadway or shoulder." (Parallel requirements apply to Preferential Lane warning signs and guide signs.) Options (permitted): - If the vertical clearance of other structures along the roadway near the sign structure is less than 16 feet, the vertical clearance to an overhead sign structure or support may be as low as 1 foot higher than the vertical clearance of the other structures in order to improve visibility of the overhead signs. [shown on Page 100 image] - In special cases the clearance to overhead signs may be reduced if necessary because of substandard dimensions in tunnels and other major structures such as double-deck bridges. [shown on Page 100 image] Visual evidence: [Image 1] Figure 2A-2, Panel H ("Overhead sign"), graphically depicts the 17 ft MIN vertical clearance from the pavement to the bottom of the overhead sign, along with the 6 ft MIN lateral offset of the support beyond the shoulder. [Image 2] shows the Section 2A.15 Standard text requiring the 17-foot minimum vertical clearance over the entire width of the pavement and shoulders, together with the associated Options for reduced clearance. [Image 5] shows Sections 2E.19–2E.20 on overhead sign installations, noting that vertical clearance of overhead signs is governed by Section 2A.15 and that overhead sign supports require a 6-foot lateral offset. [Image 3] and [Image 4] show Figure 2D-10 examples of overhead signs at an intersection but do not indicate clearance dimensions. gold_answer: At least 17 feet, except where nearby structures or special constrained structures qualify for the specific exceptions in Section 2A.15.
